ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A block of mass $m = 2 \mathrm{kg}$ starts from rest and moves upwards along an inclined plane under the action of an upward pulling force F parallel to the incline. The pulling force is removed at $t = 0.5 \mathrm{s}$. The velocity of the block as a function of time is measured using a velocity sensor, as shown in Figure B (v-t graph). The acceleration due to gravity, g, is taken as $10 \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^2$.

1. What is the magnitude of the displacement, s, of the block during the interval 0-1s?
2. What is the total distance, L, traveled by the block during the interval 0-1s?
3. Determine the angle of inclination, $\alpha$, of the inclined plane.
4. What is the magnitude of the pulling force, F?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In Figure A, the wooden block is on an inclined plane, and the pulling force F acts on the wooden block upward along the inclined plane, so take upward along the inclined plane as the positive direction. Figure B is a velocity-time graph, and the broken line approximately passes through four points: (0,0), (0.5 s, 3 m/s), (0.75 s, 0), (1 s, -1 m/s). Among them, from 0 to 0.75 s the velocity is positive, indicating that the wooden block is still moving upward along the inclined plane; from 0.75 to 1 s the velocity is negative, indicating that the wooden block moves downward along the inclined plane. Reasoning calculation: Displacement equals the signed area of the v-t graph. The area from 0 to 0.5 s is (1/2)(0.5)(3)=0.75 m; the area from 0.5 to 0.75 s is (1/2)(0.25)(3)=0.375 m; the area from 0.75 to 1 s is below the time axis, and is -(1/2)(0.25)(1)=-0.125 m. Therefore the signed displacement from 0 to 1 s is 0.75+0.375-0.125=1.0 m, and the magnitude of displacement s=1.0 m. The total distance takes the sum of the absolute values of the areas: L=0.75+0.375+0.125=1.25 m. Obtain acceleration from the slope of the v-t graph: from 0 to 0.5 s, a1=(3-0)/0.5=6 m/s^2; from 0.5 to 0.75 s, the pulling force has been removed and the wooden block is still moving upward, a2=(0-3)/0.25=-12 m/s^2; from 0.75 to 1 s, the wooden block slides downward, a3=(-1-0)/0.25=-4 m/s^2. Let the magnitude of resistance or kinetic friction be f. When it is still moving upward after the pulling force is removed, both the component of gravity along the inclined plane and the friction force are downward along the inclined plane, so a2=-(g sin α+f/m)=-12, that is g sin α+f/m=12. When the wooden block reverses direction and slides downward, the component of gravity along the inclined plane is downward and the friction force is upward, so a3=-(g sin α-f/m)=-4, that is g sin α-f/m=4. Adding the two equations gives 2g sin α=16, so g sin α=8. Take g=10 m/s^2, sin α=0.8, therefore α≈53°. Subtracting the two equations gives 2f/m=8, so f/m=4 m/s^2. From 0 to 0.5 s the pulling force F is upward, and the component of gravity along the inclined plane and the friction force are downward, therefore a1=F/m-g sin α-f/m. Substituting a1=6, m=2 kg, g sin α=8, f/m=4, obtain 6=F/2-8-4, so F/2=18, F=36 N.
